text:
Maya: Heads-up - started seeing microburst tail spikes on host ingress when serving streaming responses with small chunks. p95 jumps ~30-40ms every few minutes. Happened after kernel selector tweak earlier today, cc @Ryan @Sophia :eyes:
Ryan: ugh. Any correlating signals in kvcache or batching? link to flamegraph?
Maya: quick dump attached inline. main hotspot is host-preproc writev/syscalls and parse() path. Also noticed more tiny writes (~64-256B) which lines up with small chunking increase.
Maya: ```
# pprof top -cum host_preproc:parse
25.4%  host_preproc::parse
18.1%  syscalls::writev
12.3%  grpc::streaming_frame_assemble
 8.9%  kvcache::lookup (miss path)
```
Sophia: interesting — kernel selector change pushed a new kernel variant that prefers shorter kernel loops for low-Latency small seqs. That can reduce per-token cost for short seqs but it fragments outputs more aggressively. More fragments => more writev calls => kvcache churn when KV prefetch isn't aligned.
perf-bot: deploy:kernel-selector:v3 rolled out at 1742555400 to canary hosts (10% traffic).
deploy-bot: reverting kernel-selector:v3 on hosts: canary rollback triggered at 1742555480 (manual).
Ryan: can you grab kvcache stats for the window around the spikes? evictions, lookup latency, prefetch hit rate?
Maya: ran kvcache_tool while reproing, results below:
```
$ ./kvcache_tool stats --since 1742555200 --until 1742555600
lookups: 1.2M
hits: 810k (67%)
evictions: 42k (spike aligned with tail)
prefetch_success: 54%
avg_lookup_ms: 0.35 -> 0.9 during spike
```
Sophia: 67% hit + evictions rising explains the extra work. More fragmented streaming causes different key access patterns (short prefixes repeated) so the hotset shifts and backpressure from writev slows parsing.
Ian: proposal: try an interim batching heuristic and kvcache backoff: reduce max_batch_time_ms to force slightly bigger grouping of chunks and enable kv_prefetch with conservative window. sample config:```yaml
batching:
  max_tokens: 2048
  max_batch_time_ms: 6
  prefer_longer_sequences: true
kvcache:
  prefetch: true
  prefetch_window: 64
  eviction_backoff_ms: 50
```
Maya: spun a quick canary with those params on same canary hosts for 5 min. numbers: p50 steady, p95 dropped from +40ms spikes to +12ms, writev syscalls down ~45%.
Ryan: nice. Any downsides on throughput?
Maya: throughput slightly lower (~3%) on small-request streams but unit cost improved because CPU jitter reduced.
Sophia: sounds like a net win for our typical workload mix. We should also add a small change in kernel selector to avoid aggressive micro-op unrolling for streaming frames when chunk_size < 512. That will avoid the fragmentation at source.
Ian: opened PR #832 to add adaptive kv prefetch/backoff and batching override for streaming endpoints. Link: https://git.redwood/infra/PR/832 :thumbsup:
Ryan: can we add a tiny perf test simulating high small-chunk streaming to CI? would catch regressions earlier.
Maya: yep added a stress harness to the canary job. locally reproduces within 2 minutes.
Sophia: also adding trace annotations for kvcache misses + writev counts so we can correlate without full pprof.
Maya: thanks all. Will keep the canary running through EOD and open a postmortem if rollback needed. For now reverting cluster-wide change until kernel tweak lands. :memo: 
Ian: noted, I'll follow up on the kernel patch and link the bench results.
perf-bot: experiment:kernel-batching-adaptive started at 1742555590 on canary group.
Maya: updates tomorrow AM. :coffee:
